cards.design_implication: If investigating BEC stability mechanisms, the design should include a method to induce instability via attractive interactions rather than solely observing static properties.
does_not_establish: The quantitative value of the interaction strength.
The detailed physical process of atom ejection.
Whether other mechanisms contribute to instability.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The point of instability of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) due to attractive interactions was studied.
limitations: The text does not specify the theoretical model used to define the mechanism.
Abstract-level evidence does not provide details on the specific experimental apparatus.
cards.statement: The point of instability of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) due to attractive interactions was studied.

cards.design_implication: Experimental designs targeting this phenomenon may utilize Feshbach resonance to tune interaction strengths dynamically in 85Rb systems.
does_not_establish: The exact protocol parameters for the Feshbach resonance sweep rate.
The generalizability of this design to other atomic species.
The calibration of the magnetic fields used for the resonance.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Stable 85Rb BECs were created and then caused to collapse by slowly changing the atom-atom interaction from repulsive to attractive using a Feshbach resonance.
limitations: Specific species (85Rb) is required for this design element.
The abstract does not describe the initial creation method or the specific timing of the 'slow change'.
cards.statement: Stable 85Rb BECs were created and then caused to collapse by slowly changing the atom-atom interaction from repulsive to attractive using a Feshbach resonance.

cards.design_implication: Measurement systems should be capable of detecting abrupt transitions characterized by the ejection of atoms from the condensate.
does_not_establish: The sensitivity thresholds of the imaging or detection instruments.
The number resolution of the atom counting technique.
Whether this ejection mechanism applies to all types of condensate collapse.
cards.evidence_excerpt: At a critical value, an abrupt transition was observed in which atoms were ejected from the condensate.
limitations: The specific detection method for 'ejected atoms' is not described.
The definition of 'abrupt' is not quantified in terms of time or spatial resolution.
cards.statement: At a critical value, an abrupt transition was observed in which atoms were ejected from the condensate.

cards.design_implication: Experimental boundaries for stability should consider the measured threshold of ~0.459 for the normalized interaction parameter, acknowledging the discrepancy with the theoretical prediction of 0.574.
does_not_establish: The universal applicability of this stability condition to other trap geometries.
The specific definition of a(ho) (oscillator length related parameter) without fulltext access.
The cause of the discrepancy between the measured value and the theoretical prediction.
cards.evidence_excerpt: By measuring the onset of this transition as a function of number and attractive interaction strength, we determined the stability condition to be N(absolute value of a) / a(ho) = 0.459+/-0.012+/-0.054, slightly lower than the predicted value of 0.574.
limitations: This is an abstract-level report of a specific result, not a comprehensive review of boundary conditions across different studies.
The variables 'N', 'a', and 'a(ho)' are assumed to be defined in the full text but not in the abstract.
The uncertainty ranges include both statistical (+/-0.012) and systematic (+/-0.054) components, implying complex error analysis not detailed here.
cards.statement: The study determined a stability condition of N(absolute value of a) / a(ho) = 0.459+/-0.012+/-0.054, slightly lower than the predicted value of 0.574.
